chapters.title: History Unit 1: What is History?
chapters.description: Definition from Historia, pre-history, archaeological and literary sources, Emperor Ashoka and the Dharma Chakra.

concepts.title: What is History & Archaeological Sources
concepts.summary: History is the systematic study of the past based on inscriptions, coins, monuments, and literary records.
key_points: The term History is derived from Greek word Historia, meaning learning by inquiry.
Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga war and spread message of peace.
The 24-spoke Dharma Chakra on the Indian national flag is taken from Ashoka's Sarnath pillar.

chapters.title: History Unit 2: Human Evolution
chapters.description: Stages of human evolution from Australopithecus to Homo sapiens, discovery of fire, invention of wheel, and cave rock art.

concepts.title: Stages of Human Evolution & Prehistoric Life
concepts.summary: The journey of mankind from hunter-gatherers using stone tools and fire to settled agrarian communities.
key_points: Homo habilis made primitive stone tools; Homo erectus discovered fire using flint stones.
Invention of the potters wheel revolutionized transport, food storage, and early craftsmanship.
Prehistoric rock paintings in caves depict hunting expeditions and community life.

chapters.title: History Unit 3: Indus Civilisation
chapters.description: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, grid planned towns, Great Bath, granaries, drainage systems, Lothal dockyard.

concepts.title: Indus Valley Civilisation Town Planning
concepts.summary: Advanced urban civilisation characterized by grid-pattern streets, covered drainage systems, and the Great Bath.
key_points: Harappa was discovered in 1920 in Punjab; Mohenjo-daro in Sindh.
Streets were laid out on a grid system with right-angle intersections.
Drains were covered with stone slabs or bricks and connected to street mains.
Lothal was a prominent port and dockyard city on the Sabarmati river in Gujarat.

chapters.title: History Unit 4: Ancient Cities of Tamilagam
chapters.description: Sangam port city of Poompuhar, Pandya trade capital of Madurai (Naalangadi and Allangadi), and temple learning center Kanchi.

concepts.title: Poompuhar, Madurai & Kanchi
concepts.summary: Flourishing ancient trade, literary hubs, and learning centers in historical Tamil Nadu.
key_points: Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam) was a bustling maritime port engaged in overseas trade with Rome and Greece.
Madurai, the city of Tamil Sangam, had two distinct markets: Naalangadi (day market) and Allangadi (night market).
Kanchi was a celebrated seat of education and Buddhist learning visited by Chinese traveler Xuanzang.

chapters.title: Geography Unit 1: The Universe and Solar System
chapters.description: Big Bang, Milky Way, Sun and eight planets, terrestrial vs gas giants, rotation and revolution, and four spheres of Earth.

concepts.title: The Solar System & Planetary Motions
concepts.summary: The Sun at the center with eight planets; rotation causes day and night while revolution causes seasons.
key_points: The Solar System formed 4.6 billion years ago and resides in the Milky Way galaxy.
Inner terrestrial planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (rocky surfaces).
Outer gas giants: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Earth's rotation on its tilted axis takes 24 hours; revolution around the Sun takes 365.25 days.

chapters.title: Geography Unit 2: Land and Oceans
chapters.description: First order landforms (7 continents and 5 oceans), second order landforms (mountains, plateaus, plains), and third order landforms.

concepts.title: Continents, Oceans & Landform Classification
concepts.summary: Hierarchical orders of physical geographical relief on planet Earth.
key_points: First-order landforms: 7 Continents (Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia) and 5 Oceans.
Second-order landforms: Mountains, Plateaus (e.g. Tibetan Plateau - Roof of the World), and Plains.
Third-order landforms: Valleys, gorges, sand dunes, and deltas created by erosion and deposition.

chapters.title: Civics Unit 1: Understanding Diversity
chapters.description: Geographical, linguistic, religious, and cultural diversity in India, 8th schedule official languages, and unity in diversity.

concepts.title: Unity in Diversity & Indian Pluralism
concepts.summary: Celebrating India's rich cultural, linguistic, and geographical tapestry unified as one nation.
key_points: India is recognized for physical diversity across Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, and Coastal Ghats.
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognizes 22 official languages.
The phrase 'Unity in Diversity' was coined by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru in The Discovery of India.

chapters.title: Civics Unit 2: Achieving Equality
chapters.description: Prejudices, stereotypes, constitutional guarantees (Article 14, Article 17), and contributions of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

concepts.title: Equality & The Indian Constitution
concepts.summary: Constitutional provisions guarantee fundamental equality and outlaw discrimination in India.
key_points: Article 14 ensures equality before the law and equal protection of laws.
Article 17 completely abolishes the practice of untouchability.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution Drafting Committee and is known as the Father of Indian Constitution.
